entities.name: Lucius Genucius Aventinensis
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Genucius Aventinensis, a nobleman of ancient Rome of the Genucia gens, played a pivotal role in Roman history during the 4th century BC. As one of the two consuls of Rome in 365 BC, alongside Quintus Servilius Ahala, he contributed to the stability and governance of the Roman Republic.

Born into a prominent family, Lucius Genucius Aventinensis rose through the ranks of Roman society, eventually becoming a consul. His leadership and strategic decisions had a lasting impact on the Roman state, shaping its future for generations to come.

The legacy of Lucius Genucius Aventinensis extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing the course of Roman history and leaving behind a lasting cultural footprint.

"The Roman Senate, in its wisdom, has seen fit to recognize the achievements of Lucius Genucius Aventinensis, a true statesman and leader of unimpeachable character." - Quintus Fabius Maximus, Roman statesman and historian
